newsitem.title: UK: FCA! agency to expand in Europe after KWS merger.
newsitem.headline: FCA! agency to expand in Europe after KWS merger.

text.p: FCA! advertising agency says its recent merger with a UK-based branding specialist will help it grow across Europe and satisfy growing client demand for "through-the-line" service.
Impact FCA! in London was renamed FCA! after a part of its French parent company, Publicis SA, bought Kelly Weedon Shute agency in July.

FCA! is one of the few advertising agencies in London that specialises not only in television, cinema and print ads -- or "above-the-line" advertising -- but also "below-the-line" services such as direct marketing and sales promotion.

Chris Parry, chairman and chief executive of FCA!, says his agency has enjoyed "meteoric growth" in recent years because companies are spending increasingly on direct marketing rather than more glamorous and more expensive above-the-line advertising.
"We've established in the UK that more and more clients are looking for a 'through-the-line' solution. Clients are crying out for it," he told Reuters late on Thursday.
He said FCA! was the "first European through-the-line agency", with 17 offices in 14 countries.
The group has grown from 20 million pounds ($31.8 million) in billings in 1993 to 90 million pounds following its merger in July with Kelly Weedon Shute.

Industry experts say companies selling consumer-related products or services are increasingly reluctant to spend lots of money on television advertising because the growth of cable and satellite TV makes it tougher to reach large numbers of consumers.
Companies also find it easier to track whether direct marketing or sales promotion campaigns produce sales -- something that is more difficult to quantify with television commercials.
"It's about time advertising agencies wake up to the fact that they have to be able to deliver what the client wants," Parry said.
Because of the rapid growth of direct marketing, many above-the-line agencies have hired direct marketing specialists or created new below-the-line departments.

But Shaun McIlrath, FCA!'s joint creative director, said many of those agencies were unfamiliar or felt uncomfortable with direct marketing and continued to press clients to spend money on traditional advertising.
"Advertising agencies are in the business of selling advertising" rather than the best solution for a client, including below-the-line options, he said.
Ian Harding, FCA!'s other creative director, said above-the-line agencies had a hard time moving into direct marketing because it was considered less glamorous than traditional advertising.
"There's always been a class snobbery about advertising agencies...For the ad agencies, moving down to direct marketing is like admitting failure," he said.
As a result, "direct marketing agencies are moving up in the ranks" by winning business that used to go solely to above-the-line agencies, Harding said.
FCA!'s clients include Siemens AG, the German industrial group, Henkel KGaA, the German speciality chemicals group, and Rothmans International.
